enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

404 AM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 355 AM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

 - Easterly winds bring cooler temperatures early Monday morning and
   create breezy conditions over western mountain slopes.

 - A chance of rain showers for western New Mexico and area
   mountains on Tuesday night as a storm system crosses the 
   Central Rockies. 
   
 - Temperatures bounce back through the week, with lowland highs 
   in the upper 60s/lower 70s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 926 PM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

The weak backdoor cold front has made its way into the eastern areas 
causing winds to pick up and blow out of an east-southeasterly 
pattern. These 10-20 mph winds predominantly impact our western 
mountain slopes through the day tomorrow. A fog advisory is in 
effect until 9 AM MST on the eastern slopes of the Sacs, but the 
winds should temper widespread fog development any further west. 
By morning, wind over the Lordsburg Playa will pick up as those 
easterly winds move across the area overnight. With these winds 
advecting cooler air, morning temperatures will be a few degrees 
cooler across the lowlands in spite of the ridge currently in 
place which would normally pull warmer air up out of the south. By
tomorrow afternoon, high temperatures are comparable to seasonal 
normals for this time of year, and on Tuesday our lowland 
locations will have a chance to hit 70 again.

An upper level trough moving into our area through the day Tuesday 
will tap into the southwesterly moisture. Our area mountains present 
the best chances for rain with this system late in the day. Winds 
become light and variable after this system passes until Friday when 
southwesterly winds pick up, gusting to 25-30 mph across the area. 
Temperatures are seasonable if not above normal by the end of the 
work week. Our next bout of cold air moves into the area overnight 
Friday leaving relevant precip chances north of the area as of
yet.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 355 AM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

VFR conditions expected for the entire observation period. Some
FEW060 is possible at each of the TAF sites in the early morning
hours before dissipating by afternoon. Winds 070-110 at 5 to 10
kts.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 355 AM MST Mon Nov 16 2026

Fire weather conditions remain low for the rest of the week. A
weak backdoor cold front pushes across the region tonight,
dropping temperatures out east and bringing low-end breezy winds
in the New Mexico lowlands. Light rain showers in the Sacramentos
and Gila Region are possible Tuesday by way of a passing upper-
level trough. Any rainfall will be on the lighter side of things.
Temperatures warm up to near normal by Friday. Ventilation rates
gradually improve from Poor to Very Good by week's end. Min RHs
fall from the upper 40s on Monday to the upper 20s/lower 30s by
Friday.

&&
